domain: forced displacement / annual asylum-corridor entry events
prediction_question: For an asylum corridor (country of origin O, country of asylum H) whose total government-procedure asylum applications FIRST reach at least 500 in year T0 (its entry year), will the corridor's total applications over the two following years (T0+1 and T0+2) reach at least twice the T0 total? One row per corridor, taken once at first crossing; a useful prediction enables two-year reception and processing-capacity planning for newly-arrived flows. Measured fallback design (also one-shot, decided before any score): will the crossing year's flow grow by more than 25% in T0+1.
prediction_time: Publication-lag nowcast at the annual instant: the first refresh of the UNHCR HDX global package (data.humdata.org, dataset unhcr-population-data-for-world) that carries the entry year T0's data (observed cadence: refreshes 2026-06-11/19/22 and 2026-08-20T15:33:49Z; the 2026-08-20 file carries years 2000-2025). Features are the corridor's published yearly totals for years <= T0 only. The outcome years T0+1/T0+2 are unpublished and unavailable on this channel at the instant (first published ~mid T0+2/T0+3); for historical rows the outcome window has partially elapsed at the instant - no 'window follows the instant' claim is made (the abs-visitor-arrivals-direction / unhcr-refugee-data-finder posture). Corridors entering 2025 are live strict forecasts: their whole outcome window 2026-2027 follows the 2026-08-20 instant. Dated example in notes.md (AFG->USA).
target_definition: Binary label: (corridor G/P application total in T0+1 + total in T0+2) >= 2 x corridor G/P total in T0. Source column: Number of Applications summed over Government-procedure (Procedure Type G), person-count (Application Data Type P) rows per corridor-year (the sum rule validated against BAMF in the parent record). The T0+1 and T0+2 values are the label operands and never ship as features. Observed absence: corridor row missing while the host still reports that year = 0; host silent in an outcome year = unobserved target, row excluded (19 rows measured). Eligibility (first year >= 500) is decided only from the at-instant year-T0 row - no whole-series future inclusion. Fallback label: total(T0+1) >= 1.25 x total(T0).

split_strategy: One row per corridor at its FIRST year >= 500 government-procedure applications (entry year T0); temporal splits on entry year. Primary design (cum2_2x) measured windows: train entries 2000-2014 (653 rows / 214 positives / 153 origin-entry-year events), eval 2015-2020 (230/103/83), holdout 2021-2023 (170/73/64) - outcome years must be published, so entries stop at 2023; 57 live-edge corridors (entries 2024-2025) carry no label at the 2026-08-20 instant. Both gate minimums (30 positives / 20 distinct events on eval and holdout) pass with margin. Under the parent's momentum-feature eligibility (published T0-1 value required): 363/127, 202/98, 159/72 - still passing, so construction may adopt the stricter rule. Construction may re-draw boundaries BEFORE any score is seen. Measured fallback (next1_g25, entries T0<=2024): train 709/185/136, eval 183/59/46, holdout 201/68/59. The direct analogue (one-shot + next-year 2x, the parent task's label) is measured NOT viable: eval 183/25/20, holdout 201/28/28 (below 30), zero-positive entry years 2019 and 2024.

review: Five contracts reconciled 2026-11-04 on written evidence (details and dated example in notes.md): (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - cc-by-igo re-verified live on the package today; class A; conditions carry to LICENSE.md; no unhcr.org scraping. (2) Timing SUPPORTED with the documented current-vintage assumption - annual publication-lag nowcast instant, outcome years unpublished at the instant, live 2025-entrant rows strict forecasts; the archive is revised in place so values are construction-time vintage, sha256-pinned (parent-record posture); no claim of historical operational availability of today's vintages. (3) Target SUPPORTED - label operands (T0+1/T0+2 totals) excluded from features by the one-row-per-corridor structure; observed-zero vs host-silent censoring measured; eligibility from at-instant information only. (4) Split capacity SUPPORTED with margin for the primary design (eval 103/83, holdout 73/64 vs gate 30/20; momentum-eligibility variant also passing); the direct next-year-2x analogue measured not viable (25/28) and recorded. (5) Not a mirror SUPPORTED - differentiated verdict recorded via check-novelty.py; no released corridor-grain first-crossing task with fixed splits and a scored contract exists; prior art is EU-only monthly panel forecasting or unreleased systems. LIMITATION recorded for construction: rows share origins across windows, so a later entrant's origin-level aggregate can contain components of an earlier entrant's outcome years - partial information, not the parent's exact-copy exposure; the gate 1.5.0 cross-row probe must run on the built artifact with the aggregate features declared. This record formulates the operator's recorded reopen condition (unhcr-refugee-data-finder, 2026-11-02): the one-shot design removes the adjacent-row self-answering structurally; the aggregate-outcome label is the operator's second named shape.

novelty_check.theirs: The publisher ships the raw panel (HDX global package), not a task. Prior art is EU-focused: bilateral monthly Eurostat flow forecasting (J Econ Geography 25(1):3 2025; BSE WP 1387, no dataset release), Italy-aggregate 6-month forecasting (Cambridge Data & Policy 2024), JRC122178 4-week EU system (internal), Napierala et al. 2022 cusum alert detection (EU weekly/monthly, no released benchmark), OECD Migration Anticipation and Preparedness 2025 (survey), arXiv:2505.06249 origin-grain monthly early warning (no released task), HF/Zenodo raw-panel repackages only.
novelty_check.ours: A one-row-per-corridor first-crossing benchmark on UNHCR's global asylum-applications channel (130 hosts, 215 origins, 2000-2025): predict, at the first publication of a corridor's >=500-application year, whether the corridor's flow over the next two years reaches twice that level - fixed entry-year train/eval/holdout splits, clustered event counts, a scored contract and a live strict-forecast edge. No existing release predicts corridor emergence at first crossing; nothing here ships adjacent corridor-years (the redesign of the dropped panel task).
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
